A team website consists of these parts, in this order:

1. `<header>` with the group name, tagline and theme toggle

   - `<section id="future-of-se">` – the team's shared view on AI and the future of software engineering,

Status: ACTIVE (version 3)

This style guide defines how team websites in the Agentic Software Engineering lab look and behave.
It is maintained by the (entirely fictional) UPB Web Design Board.

---

[SG-49] Responsive breakpoints (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-50
Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-50
Category: Responsive

Team websites are designed mobile-first with one breakpoint.

- Breakpoint: `@media (max-width: 600px)`
- Below the breakpoint, member cards are shown in one column.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width.

---

[SG-01] Glossary | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Meta

- **Team website**: the single HTML file that introduces one lab group.
- **Member card**: the block that introduces one team member.
- **Hot take**: a short, provocative opinion of a team member about AI.
- **Theme**: the visual mode of the page, either day (light) or night (dark).
- **Accent**: the one highlight color used for emphasis.
- **Breakpoint**: the viewport width at which the layout switches between mobile and desktop.
- **Data URI**: a way to embed a file (for example an image) directly inside the HTML.
- **Reduced motion**: a user setting in the operating system asking websites to minimise animation.

---

[SG-50] Responsive breakpoints (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Responsive

Team websites use exactly one layout breakpoint.

- The breakpoint MUST be written as `@media (max-width: 700px)`.
  The earlier, smaller breakpoint made cards too narrow on large phones.
- Below the breakpoint:
  - member cards are shown in one column
  - the header content is stacked vertically
  - side padding is reduced to 1rem
- The page MUST include `<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">`.
- Test your page at 375 px and 1280 px width. There must be no horizontal scrolling.

# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

# Nithya

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

# <First name>

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. ## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

=== Mohammad.md ===
# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

# Nithya

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

# <First name>

## Study background

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

# <First name>

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

[SG-22] Theme toggle control | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-13] Night mode palette (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Color

The night mode uses a calm dark blue instead of pure black. Pure black caused eye strain in user tests.

- Page background MUST be `#14142B` (midnight blue).
- Main text color MUST be `#F4F1DE` (soft cream).
- Secondary text SHOULD be `#B8B5A7`.
- Card background SHOULD be `#1F1F3D`.

Define these colors as CSS custom properties for the dark theme. See the theme switching document for how the theme is applied.

---

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-28] Buttons | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Components

- Buttons use the accent color for their border and text, with a transparent background.
- On hover, the background becomes the accent color and the text becomes white.
- Buttons MUST have a visible focus outline.
- The touch target of a button SHOULD be at least 44 × 44 CSS pixels.

=== Mohammad.md ===
# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.


=== Nithya.md ===
# Nithya

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.


=== Rafee.md ===
# Rafee

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Frontend UI/UX, React/Next.js ecosystem, Table Tennis, Photography

## Fun fact

I judge coffee shops entirely by their Wi-Fi stability and latency to GitHub.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

From a fresh developer perspective, AI is an unbelievable interactive tutor that demystifies obscure compiler errors in seconds. But relying on it too early is a trap: it creates an illusion of competence where you understand the output without understanding the underlying mechanics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Natural language and intent-driven wireframes will directly compile into accessible, responsive user interfaces. The frontend engineer's job will focus almost entirely on user empathy, accessibility, and high-performance client-side state rather than CSS layout fighting.

## My hot take on AI

If you can't debug code without an LLM, you are the copilot, not the agent.

# Raghvendra

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 3rd semester

## Interests

Machine Learning Infrastructure, Data Engineering, Hiking, Chess

## Fun fact

I will spend 4 hours automating a manual 5-minute task, and call it an investment.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

Current LLMs are incredible for rapid prototyping and translating business logic into SQL or boilerplate endpoints. However, they lack deep situational context and often pull in deprecated methods without warning. Their true utility is reducing initial friction, not making core architectural choices.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Developers will primarily converse with multi-agent pipelines that autonomously build, test, and benchmark microservices against synthetic workloads. Humans will intervene primarily to define objective functions, enforce privacy boundaries, and resolve conflicting business constraints.

## My hot take on AI

90% of current 'AI agent' workflows are just fragile `while` loops wrapped around regex parsers.

# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

# Nithya

## Interests

## Fun fact

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. ## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. ## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. ## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Frontend UI/UX, React/Next.js ecosystem, Table Tennis, Photography

## Fun fact

I judge coffee shops entirely by their Wi-Fi stability and latency to GitHub.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

From a fresh developer perspective, AI is an unbelievable interactive tutor that demystifies obscure compiler errors in seconds. But relying on it too early is a trap: it creates an illusion of competence where you understand the output without understanding the underlying mechanics.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Natural language and intent-driven wireframes will directly compile into accessible, responsive user interfaces. The frontend engineer's job will focus almost entirely on user empathy, accessibility, and high-performance client-side state rather than CSS layout fighting.

## My hot take on AI

If you can't debug code without an LLM, you are the copilot, not the agent.


=== Raghvendra.md ===
# Raghvendra

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 3rd semester

## Interests

Machine Learning Infrastructure, Data Engineering, Hiking, Chess

## Fun fact

I will spend 4 hours automating a manual 5-minute task, and call it an investment.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

Current LLMs are incredible for rapid prototyping and translating business logic into SQL or boilerplate endpoints. However, they lack deep situational context and often pull in deprecated methods without warning. Their true utility is reducing initial friction, not making core architectural choices.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Developers will primarily converse with multi-agent pipelines that autonomously build, test, and benchmark microservices against synthetic workloads. Humans will intervene primarily to define objective functions, enforce privacy boundaries, and resolve conflicting business constraints.

## My hot take on AI

90% of current 'AI agent' workflows are just fragile `while` loops wrapped around regex parsers.

=== Mohammad.md ===
# <First name>

Mohammad

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.


=== Nithya.md ===
# Nithya

## Study background

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

M.Sc. Computer Science, 1st semester

## Interests

Full-stack development, Gaming

## Fun fact

I’ll patiently sit through a 40-hour story-driven game with zero skips, but waiting 30 seconds for a build pipeline to finish tests my entire sanity.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI is unmatched for ripping through boilerplate and syntax lookups, but it frequently hallucinates subtle logical flaws that make debugging twice as tedious. It speeds up the typing part of programming without genuinely understanding system architecture or context. Right now, it works best as an eager junior developer whose every commit needs thorough code review.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

The core job will shift almost entirely from typing code to specifying requirements, edge cases, and architectural constraints. Writing raw boilerplate by hand will largely disappear, replaced by autonomous agents managed by engineers acting as system architects. True engineering value will center on verification, fault tolerance, and knowing what to build rather than how to type it out.

## My hot take on AI

AI doesn’t make bad developers good; it just helps them generate catastrophic technical debt at record speed.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-22] Theme toggle control | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

Status: ACTIVE (version 2)

- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

M.Sc. Computer Science, 7th semester (Thesis stage)

## Interests

Distributed Systems, Cloud Architecture, Badminton, Board games

## Fun fact

I have rewritten my thesis abstract more times than I have recompiled my actual code.

## What I think about AI in software engineering today

AI assistants are fantastic productivity multipliers for well-understood domains and boilerplate generation, but they break down when faced with complex legacy enterprise codebases. They often exhibit blind confidence on subtle synchronization primitives and concurrency issues. Right now, AI acts as a fast copilot, but you cannot let it navigate without senior oversight.

## Where software engineering will be in 5–10 years

Engineering will center heavily on systems integration, prompt-driven formal verification, and distributed consensus rather than mundane feature programming. Junior roles will evolve into system orchestration positions where knowing failure modes and domain invariants will matter far more than knowing low-level library APIs.

## My hot take on AI

AI autocomplete hasn't eliminated bugs; it has just made them compile much faster.

[SG-18] Dark mode philosophy | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

Users choose their theme, but we start with a sensible default.

- If the user has never chosen a theme, the page SHOULD follow the operating system preference (`prefers-color-scheme`).
- As soon as the user clicks the toggle, their choice wins and is remembered, see the theme persistence document.
- Switching the theme MUST NOT reload the page.

---

[SG-20] Theme switching mechanics | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

The theme is controlled by one attribute on the root element.

- The `<html>` element MUST carry the attribute `data-theme` with the value `light` or `dark`.
- JavaScript switches the theme by changing this attribute, not by toggling classes on the body.
- The CSS MUST define the colors for each theme with attribute selectors, for example
  `[data-theme="light"] { ... }` and `[data-theme="dark"] { ... }`.
- Components use CSS custom properties (for example `var(--bg)`), so they don't need theme-specific rules.

---

[SG-22] Theme toggle control | Status: ACTIVE
Status: ACTIVE
Category: Theming

- The toggle MUST be a `<button>` element with the id `theme-toggle`.
- It MUST have an `aria-label` describing the action, for example `aria-label="Switch to night mode"`.
  Update the label when the theme changes.
- It SHOULD show a sun symbol in night mode and a moon symbol in day mode.
- It SHOULD be placed in the top right corner of the header.
- Don't use a checkbox for the toggle.

---

[SG-21] Theme persistence (version 2) | Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Status: ACTIVE (version 2)
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- The choice MUST be stored in `localStorage` under the key `upb-theme`.
  The old key was too generic and collided with other local files.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- On page load, read the stored value. If there is none, follow the operating system preference.
- Apply the theme as early as possible to avoid a flash of the wrong theme.

---

[SG-19] Theme persistence (version 1) | Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
Status: DEPRECATED – replaced by SG-21
Category: Theming

The theme choice of the user is remembered between visits.

- Store the choice in `localStorage` under the key `theme`.
- The stored value is either `light` or `dark`.
- Read the value when the page loads and apply it before the first paint.
